author: Tom George
title: Russ Overton sworn in as Cary's permanent town manager after 11 months as interim - NewsBreak
text:
By Tom George ,
18 minutes ago
Russ Overton was officially sworn in as Cary's town manager Thursday, nearly a year after taking over the position on an interim basis following the resignation of former Town Manager Sean Stegall.
Overton received a round of applause during the ceremony.
"I'm incredibly proud of what we all continue to accomplish together. I believe our best days are ahead of us," Overton said.
Mayor Harold Weinbrecht said Overton's familiarity with Cary and his experience made him the right choice for the position.
"Been a tough 11 months to move this organization forward, which is a strong organization," Weinbrecht said. "We needed somebody that knows Cary very, very well. Somebody that has the experience and the knowledge to keep Cary one of the best communities in the nation."
Overton became interim town manager last December after Stegall resigned following his placement on leave. The change came in the wake of financial issues and concerns about a culture of excessive spending.
Councilmember Carissa Kohn-Johnson said Overton faced significant challenges as the town dealt with subsequent audits and investigations.
"As interim town manager. Russ Overton had absolutely no wiggle room," Kohn-Johnson said.
Council members opted against conducting a national search for a new town manager, instead choosing someone already familiar with Cary.
"And I know there were some folks that are like, well, you know, maybe you should have started from scratch. I do believe that the longevity and the continuity, this is what we need to keep our town stable and to keep delivering the services that our residents have come to expect," Kohn-Johnson said.
Overton has also been part of the team working to implement new recommendations following an audit. Measures discussed Thursday included reviewing town credit card purchases, reinstating an internal auditor position and improving oversight of town finances.
Kohn-Johnson said the changes would include greater scrutiny of spending and town policies.
"They're also going to see that there's going to be absolute concerted effort for us to question every spend, to look at every single policy we have, and make sure that our staff behavior, our council behavior, matches the policies that we have in place."
Overton's contract began Thursday immediately after the council's vote. He will be paid $344,000 a year.

Overton became interim town manager last December after Stegall resigned following his placement on leave. Councilmember Carissa Kohn-Johnson said Overton faced significant challenges as the town dealt with subsequent audits and investigations. Council members opted against conducting a national search for a new town manager, instead choosing someone already familiar with Cary.
